Q82919.label: Alessandro Rossi
Q82919.summary: Alessandro Rossi is a Sammarinese politician who served as one of the two Captains Regent of San Marino from April to October 2024, alongside Milena Gasperoni. Rossi previously served as Captain Regent from 1 April to 1 October 2007, together with Alessandro Mancini. In January 2005 Rossi was the leader of Ideas in Movement, later on 2 October 2006, Rossi would join the Council of Europe until 26 January 2009, then again on 21 January 2013, until 29 September 2013; during that time period Rossi would become a member of Group of the Unified European Left.

Q21014503.label: Danish European Union opt-out referendum, 2015
Q21014503.img: Valgplakat til Folkeafstemningen om retsforbeholdet, Nej tak.JPG
Q21014503.summary: A referendum on one of the country's opt-outs from the European Union was held in Denmark on 3 December 2015. Specifically, the referendum was on whether to convert Denmark's current full opt-out on home and justice matters into an opt-out with case-by-case opt-in similar to those held by Ireland and the United Kingdom.

Q1089511.summary: The Battle of Ras Lanuf was a two-phase battle in early to mid-March 2011 during the Libyan Civil War between forces loyal to Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi and those loyal to the National Transitional Council. Both forces sought control of the town of Ras Lanuf.

Q5375463.label: Encirclement Campaign against Northeastern Jiangxi Soviet
Q5375463.wiki: Encirclement campaign against the Northeastern Jiangxi Soviet
Q5375463.summary: The encirclement campaign against the Northeastern Jiangxi Soviet was a campaign launched by the Chinese Nationalist Government intended to destroy the communist Chinese Soviet Republic and its local military forces. It was met by the Communists' Counter-encirclement campaign at Northeastern Jiangxi Soviet, also called the Counter-encirclement campaign at Northeastern Jiangxi Revolutionary Base. The Nationalist campaign lasted from December 1930 to July 1931, and resulted in the destruction of the target base area.

Q2015719.label: Campaign of Gipuzkoa
Q2015719.desc: 1936 military campaign;part of the Spanish Civil War
Q2015719.summary: The campaign of Gipuzkoa was part of the Spanish Civil War, where the Nationalist Army conquered the northern province of Gipuzkoa, held by the Republic.

Q4885479.label: Bombing of Alicante
Q4885479.desc: 1938 aerial attack of the Spanish Civil War
Q4885479.img: Runa posterior al bombardeig del Mercat Central d'Alacant.jpg
Q4885479.summary: On 25 May 1938, the Valencian town of Alicante was aerially bombed during the Spanish Civil War. This particular attack was one of many against Alicante, perpetrated by the Legionary Air Force, an expeditionary corps from the Italian Royal Air Force, allied with Franco. The attacking planes were based in Mallorca. It is considered by historians to be one of the deadliest aerial bombings of the entire Spanish Civil War with many bombs dropped on a strictly civilian population with no military targets within a short amount of time.

Q7097319.label: Operation Neuland
Q7097319.desc: 1942 submarine warfare of the German Kriegsmarine in the Caribbean Sea
Q7097319.summary: Operation Neuland was the code name of the Kriegsmarine extension of unrestricted submarine warfare into the Caribbean Sea during World War II. German U-boats demonstrated range to disrupt British petroleum supplies and American aluminum supplies which had not been anticipated by Allied pre-war planning. Although the area remained vulnerable to submarines for several months, U-boats never again enjoyed the opportunities for success resulting from the surprise of this operation.

Q4090343.label: Shatoy ambush
Q4090343.desc: The Shatoy ambush of April 16, 1996 by forces of commander Ibn al-khattab.
Q4090343.summary: The Shatoy ambush was a significant event during the First Chechen War. It occurred near the town of Shatoy, located in the southern mountains of Chechnya. Chechen insurgents under the leadership of their Arab-born commander, Ibn al-Khattab, would launch an attack on a large Russian Armed Forces army convoy resulting in a three hour long battle.

Q981479.label: Carl Icahn
Q981479.summary: Carl Celian Icahn is an American businessman and investor. He is the founder and controlling shareholder of Icahn Enterprises, a public company and diversified conglomerate holding company based in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida. Icahn's business model is to take large stakes in companies that he believes will appreciate from changes to corporate policy; Icahn then pressures management to make the changes that he believes will benefit shareholders, and him.

Q1995239.label: Sushruta Samhita
Q1995239.desc: sushruta samhita is an ancient sanskrit text on medicine
Q1995239.img: Page of text from the Susrutasamhita Wellcome L0034908.jpg
Q1995239.summary: The Sushruta Samhita is an ancient Sanskrit text on medicine and one of the most important such treatises on this subject to survive from the ancient world. The Compendium of Suśruta is one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda, alongside the Charaka-Saṃhitā, the Bhela-Saṃhitā, and the medical portions of the Bower Manuscript. It is one of two foundational Hindu texts on the medical profession that have survived from ancient India.

Q9191.label: René Descartes
Q9191.img: Frans Hals - Portret van René Descartes.jpg
Q9191.summary: René Descartes was a French philosopher, mathematician, and scientist whose work was foundational to mathematics and modern philosophy, and influenced the development of early modern science. He connected the previously separate fields of geometry and algebra into analytic geometry, introduced a systematic method of inquiry that became influential in early modern philosophy, and made major contributions to epistemology and philosophy of mind as well as metaphysics.

mentions.c: Descartes and Fermat unite algebra and geometry (1637)

Q8063463.label: Zabdiel Boylston
Q8063463.desc: American physician and the first inoculator for smallpox in the United States (1679-1766)
Q8063463.summary: Zabdiel Boylston, FRS was a physician in the Boston area. As the first medical school in North America was not founded until 1765, Boylston apprenticed with his father, a surgeon named Thomas Boylston, and studied under the Boston physician Dr. Cutler. Boylston is known for holding several "firsts" for an American-born physician: he performed the first surgical operation by an American physician, the first removal of gall bladder stones in 1710, and the first removal of a breast tumor in 1718. He was also the first physician to perform smallpox inoculations in North America.

mentions.c: Onesimus’s inoculation saves lives in Boston (1721)

Q334311.label: St Thomas's Abbey in Brno
Q334311.summary: St Thomas's Abbey is an Augustinian abbey and church located in Brno in the Czech Republic. The geneticist and abbot Gregor Mendel was its most famous religious leader to date, who between 1856 and 1863 conducted his experiments on pea plants in the monastery garden. His experiments brought forth two generalizations which later became known as Mendel's Laws of Inheritance.

Q310759.summary: Henry Gwyn Jeffreys Moseley was an English physicist, whose contribution to the science of physics was the justification from physical laws of the previous empirical and chemical concept of the atomic number. This stemmed from his development of Moseley's law in X-ray spectra.

Q750567.label: Spring Offensive
Q750567.desc: 1918 series of German attacks along the Western Front during the First World War
Q750567.img: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-P1013-316, Westfront, deutscher Panzer in Roye.jpg
Q750567.summary: The German spring offensive, also known as Kaiserschlacht or the Ludendorff offensive, was a series of German attacks along the Western Front during the First World War, beginning on 21 March 1918. Following the American entry into the war in April 1917, the Germans decided that their only remaining chance of victory was to defeat the Allies before the United States could ship soldiers across the Atlantic and fully deploy its resources.

Q1511.label: Richard Wagner
Q1511.summary: Wilhelm Richard Wagner was a German composer, theatre director, essayist, and conductor, best known for his operas, although his mature works are often referred to as music dramas. Unlike most composers, Wagner wrote both the libretti and the music for all of his stage works. He first achieved recognition with works in the Romantic tradition of Carl Maria von Weber and Giacomo Meyerbeer, but revolutionised the genre through his concept of the Gesamtkunstwerk, which sought to unite poetic, musical, visual, and dramatic elements.

Q1661415.label: green politics
Q1661415.desc: political ideology that aims to create an ecologically sustainable society rooted in environmentalism, social justice, and grassroots democracy
Q1661415.summary: Green politics, or ecopolitics, is a political ideology that aims to foster an ecologically sustainable society often, but not always, rooted in environmentalism, nonviolence, social justice and grassroots democracy. It began taking shape in the Western world in the 1970s; since then, green parties have developed and established themselves in many countries around the globe and have achieved some electoral success.
